findings.title: Requests are no longer rejected after Stop()
findings.body: `Stop` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped" (lines 321, 328, 339). The only thing that turned that into a request error was the `s.Init(ctx)` call at the top of every handler, and this PR removed all of those calls (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob). After Stop, `s.cancel()` has run and the backend is stopped, yet handlers now run against it and fail with arbitrary backend or context errors, or hang in Watch. `initErr` is now written by `Stop` and read by nothing but `Init`'s return value, so those assignments do nothing. Add an explicit stopped/initErr check to the handlers, for example one shared helper, or drop the dead assignments and accept the new behaviour on purpose.

findings.title: Init now runs eagerly inside NewResourceServer; startup failure and ordering change
findings.body: Init, which runs `lifecycle.Init` (SQL backend `dbProvider.Init` + Ping), `search.init` (a full index build via `GetResourceStats` and `ListIterator`) and `initWatcher`, now runs synchronously in the constructor. It used to run lazily on the first request. Any DB or index failure now makes `NewResourceServer` return an error, so startup is blocked and `sql.NewResourceServer` (`pkg/storage/unified/sql/server.go:77`), `apistore/restoptions.go` and `client.go` all fail. Two questions: (1) Are the resource tables guaranteed to exist at every call site, for example the apiserver `restoptions` path, which may run before migrations? (2) Is blocking startup on a full index build intended? The postgres skip added in `pkg/server/module_server_test.go` makes me wonder whether this is the cause. Also, on this error return (and the earlier ones after line 229) the `cancel` for `s.ctx` is never called, so the context leaks.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu.RLock()`. `BuildIndex` writes the map under `cacheMu.Lock()` (lines 137-139). It is called from the Prometheus collector (`bleve_index_metrics.go:96`) and, with this PR, from `searchSupport.init` (`search.go:216`). It can run at the same time as a `BuildIndex` triggered by `getOrCreateIndex`, which gives a concurrent map read and write (a fatal runtime error in Go). The race existed before, but this PR adds a caller and narrows the lock window rather than fixing the read side. Take `RLock` in `TotalDocs`.

findings.title: BuildIndex no longer serialized; same-key concurrent builds are unguarded
findings.body: Removing the lock held for all of `BuildIndex` stops `GetIndex` readers from blocking during a build, which is the intended speedup. But `getOrCreateIndex` (`search.go:287-307`) has no per-key guard. Two concurrent searches for a missing key now both run `bleve.New(dir)`/build in parallel. For file-backed indexes the second `bleve.New` fails on the existing directory. For memory indexes, both build in full and the last writer overwrites the cache entry, orphaning the other. Consider a per-key singleflight or re-check the cache under the lock before inserting.

findings.title: Test skipped for postgres rather than fixed
findings.body: The test is disabled for postgres on the grounds that it "works locally" in Drone. This PR moves resource-server init into the constructor, which changes startup behaviour for this storage-server target. Please confirm the failure is not caused by that change. Otherwise the skip hides a regression in the one test that covers the storage server target on postgres.

contracts.action: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) eagerly with the internal watcher/admin context
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously every handler called s.Init(ctx) lazily (sync.Once) with the request context
contracts.before_after: Before: first request ran lifecycle.Init, initWatcher, search.init using the request ctx, and errors were returned per request. After: it runs once at construction with the admin 'watcher' ctx. Errors fail construction. Handlers no longer check initErr, which Stop sets.
contracts.visible_effect: Startup takes as long as the index build; init failure aborts server construction; post-Stop requests are no longer rejected
contracts.failure_mode: Init error returns nil,err and leaks s.cancel. After Stop, handlers proceed against a stopped backend.

contracts.action: Moved cacheMu locking in bleveBackend.BuildIndex to only the cache insert; added TotalDocs call in search init log
contracts.equivalent_path: GetIndex takes RLock; TotalDocs takes no lock
contracts.before_after: Before: BuildIndex held the write lock for the whole build, blocking GetIndex. After: only the map write is locked, so builds can overlap, and TotalDocs still reads the map unlocked.
contracts.visible_effect: Searches no longer block on unrelated index builds; possible duplicate builds for the same key
contracts.failure_mode: Concurrent map read/write in TotalDocs (metrics collector or init log) against BuildIndex insert; file-index build for same key fails on existing dir

summary: The PR moves resource-server init into `NewResourceServer`, removes the per-request `Init` calls, and narrows the bleve cache lock. The main defect is that `Stop` sets `initErr` to reject requests, and the removed `Init` calls were the only thing that enforced it, so handlers now run after Stop. Other points: `TotalDocs` still reads the cache map without a lock (and gains a caller), same-key concurrent builds are unguarded now that `BuildIndex` no longer holds the lock, eager init changes startup failure behaviour, and a postgres test skip may hide a regression. The tracing `ctx` reassignments and the logger swap look fine.
